summary: IDS feed s152_double is degraded: 8.5% TCP packet drops and sustained tool overload (1.46 Gbps bursts vs 1 Gbps port, 146% capacity) causing incomplete traffic delivery and missed detections.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker/SPAN aggregation dropping under load: 155 of 1828 TCP packets (8.48% vs 1% threshold) show missing data/gaps, correlated with microbursts that exceed the 1 Gbps IDS port capacity.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS needs full payload and both directions for TCP stream reassembly and signature matching; gaps cause failed reassembly, evasion of detection, and false negatives.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across 2 IDS ports/instances with flow-aware hashing to keep per-port utilization below 80% and eliminate broker-level drops while preserving flow symmetry required by IDS.

findings.root_cause: Single 1 Gbps IDS port oversubscribed by packet broker: peak 1.46 Gbps in 1 ms burst (146% of capacity) across 5 overloaded intervals with no load balancing or filtering.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS NIC buffers overflow during bursts, dropping traffic exactly when inspection is most needed; results in blind spots and degraded detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Hash-based load balancing preserves bidirectional flow affinity required by IDS and keeps each 1 Gbps tool port under 80% threshold, preventing burst drops.
